cx_score.definition: 100*(0.5*review + 0.3*delivery + 0.2*text sentiment); if no text: 100*(0.65*review + 0.35*delivery). review=(stars-1)/4; delivery=1 if on time else 1-delay/14 (floored 0); sentiment=1-P(negative) from out-of-fold TF-IDF model.

order_structure.note: Multi-item orders may be delivered in parts and a single review covers all items (dataset limitation); association only.

recommendations.action: Treat late delivery as the top operational KPI: set an alert when an order passes its estimated date and trigger proactive customer communication, and make the estimated-date promise more realistic.
recommendations.why: 62.4% of late orders are dissatisfied vs 9.3% on time (odds ratio 16.3); in the controlled logistic model lateness keeps an odds ratio of 7.7. Delivery features are the largest SHAP factor group.
recommendations.expected_impact: Association-based range: roughly 1,011 (reviews written after delivery only) to 3,392 (all reviews) fewer dissatisfied reviews among 6,381 late orders if lateness were eliminated. This is an upper-bound association, not a proven causal effect.
recommendations.measure: Weekly late-delivery rate; dissatisfied-review rate for late vs on-time orders; share of late orders contacted before the estimated date.

recommendations.action: Review the high-revenue / low-experience 'priority problem' sellers first: agree improvement plans on handling time and shipping-deadline compliance, with a probation threshold.
recommendations.why: Seller dissatisfaction rates differ significantly (chi-square p=2e-235, Cramer's V=0.17); 98 of 413 sellers with >= 50 orders are in the priority-problem segment; top examples: 4a3ca931.. (1707 orders, avg 3.89), 7c67e144.. (960 orders, avg 3.50), 1025f0e2.. (891 orders, avg 4.02)
recommendations.expected_impact: Because these sellers carry high order volume, each point of improvement reaches more customers than fixes for low-volume sellers.
recommendations.measure: Per-seller average score, late rate and dissatisfied rate (with 95% CI) monthly; movement between segments.

recommendations.action: Investigate high-revenue categories with below-average satisfaction (watches_gifts, bed_bath_table, computers_accessories): product descriptions, size/dimension accuracy, packaging and carrier choice for bulky items.
recommendations.why: 9 of 52 categories are significantly worse than the overall dissatisfied rate; the top worst categories by rate are fashion_male_clothing, office_furniture, audio.
recommendations.expected_impact: Targets categories where revenue is large, so reduced dissatisfaction protects the most sales.
recommendations.measure: Category dissatisfied rate and complaint mix (damaged/quality/wrong product) per month.

recommendations.action: Run a regional logistics review for hotspot states (AL, MA, SE, RJ): carrier performance, realistic delivery estimates, and local fulfilment options.
recommendations.why: 9 of 24 states have a dissatisfied rate whose 95% CI lies above the overall rate; hotspots include AL (21.3% dissatisfied, 20.8% late, n=394); MA (19.9% dissatisfied, 17.1% late, n=712); SE (18.9% dissatisfied, 15.0% late, n=334); RJ (18.3% dissatisfied, 11.9% late, n=12211).
recommendations.expected_impact: Fixing high-volume hotspots (e.g. RJ) affects many orders; smaller states show higher rates but fewer customers.
recommendations.measure: State-level late rate, delivery days vs estimate, dissatisfied rate with CI.

recommendations.action: Audit multi-item and multi-seller orders: check for partial/split shipments and communicate which items arrive separately.
recommendations.why: Orders with 2+ items have 26.7% dissatisfied vs 11.3% for single-item orders; 'items in order' is the 2nd most important feature in the delivery-time SHAP model. The gap persists among ON-TIME orders (24.6% vs 7.5%), so it is not just lateness. Complaint text also shows missing/partial deliveries (12.7% of negative reviews).
recommendations.expected_impact: Addresses a driver independent of lateness; size of effect depends on how much is due to split shipments (not observable here).
recommendations.measure: Dissatisfied rate by item count; share of orders delivered in one shipment; 'missing product' complaint share.

recommendations.action: Improve seller/store responsiveness (reply SLA for complaints, exchange and refund handling).
recommendations.why: Seller-issue complaints appear in 17.0% of negative commented reviews and have the lowest mean score (1.83). Caveat: this category had the weakest classifier precision in our evaluation.
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduces escalations (e.g. consumer-complaint sites mentioned in reviews).
recommendations.measure: Median response time; share of complaints resolved; seller_issue complaint rate.

recommendations.action: Do not assume that fixing ratings alone will raise repeat purchases; test retention interventions (e.g. coupons after a bad experience) with an A/B experiment.
recommendations.why: Repeat rate after a dissatisfied first order was 3.77% vs 4.10% after a satisfied one (p=0.19): no significant difference, and only 3.1% of customers ever reorder in this data.
recommendations.expected_impact: Avoids investing in a retention effect the data does not support.
recommendations.measure: Repeat-purchase rate within 180 days by experience group in a controlled experiment.

findings.finding: Late deliveries are strongly associated with dissatisfied reviews.
findings.evidence: 62.4% of late orders vs 9.3% of on-time orders are 1-2 stars (Cliff's delta -0.64); dissatisfaction rises from 12% (on the estimated day) to 80% (8-14 days late). Restricted to reviews written after delivery the effect is smaller (delta -0.30) because many late-order reviews were written before the recorded delivery.
findings.business_impact: 6,381 late orders (6.7% of reviewed orders) generate a disproportionate share of dissatisfaction.

findings.finding: Customers mainly complain about non-delivery/delay, incomplete orders and seller responsiveness - not price.
findings.evidence: Late/not-delivered appears in 40.3% of negative commented reviews; price and freight effects are negligible (Cliff's delta -0.04 and -0.04).
findings.business_impact: Operational fixes matter more than discounting.

findings.finding: Seller quality is heterogeneous: a set of sellers is significantly worse than the platform.
findings.evidence: 52 of 413 sellers (>=50 orders) have a dissatisfaction CI entirely above the overall rate (chi-square p=2e-235).

findings.finding: Some high-revenue categories and several regions under-perform.
findings.evidence: 9 categories and 9 states are significantly worse than overall; effect sizes are small (Cramer's V 0.07 and 0.09).

findings.finding: Multi-item orders are a hidden risk factor.
findings.evidence: 26.7% vs 11.3% dissatisfied; 2nd most important SHAP feature in the delivery-time model.

findings.finding: Predicting dissatisfaction is hard from structured data alone; delivery outcome and seller history are what help.
findings.evidence: See ML results: checkout-time ROC-AUC about 0.57-0.61, delivery-time about 0.69-0.71; historical review features add a significant but modest gain.
findings.business_impact: Use the model for risk monitoring, not individual decisions.

findings.finding: No evidence in this dataset that a bad experience reduces repeat purchase.
findings.evidence: Repeat rate 3.77% vs 4.10% (p=0.19); only 3.1% of customers reorder.
